option_relations.rationale: Epithelioid hemangioma is a distinct benign vascular tumor characterized by epithelioid endothelial cells, often associated with inflammation, which does not match the description of targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
Morpheaform hemangioma is a rare, infiltrative vascular tumor with a sclerotic stroma, which is not consistent with the features of targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
Microvenular hemangioma (MVH) is an alternative name for targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma, describing the same clinical entity.
Tufted angioma is a benign vascular tumor characterized by cannonball-like tufts of capillaries, which is histologically distinct from targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
